_why: Skill-candidates row 'hook-tests-run-under-the-wrong-interpreter': the suite drives the TDD gate hooks with sys.executable while the live launch resolves python3 from PATH. These rows prove the live-interpreter smoke set bites: each hook's unresolvable-target refusal, that the launch really goes through PATH's python3 (not sys.executable), and that the file skips, naming the interpreter, when the run would be vacuous.

mutations.name: codex-symlink-loop-target-allowed
mutations._mechanism: A loop target slips past the codex hook's unresolvable refusal and is allowed.
mutations.find: return _deny(f"H-MAD Phase 5 target is unresolvable ({resolved.component}); refusing fail-closed. kind=judge-error")

mutations.name: agy-symlink-loop-target-allowed
mutations._mechanism: A loop target slips past the agy hook's unresolvable refusal.

mutations.name: agy-launched-through-sys-executable
mutations._mechanism: The agy hook is driven by the suite's interpreter, so the shebang no longer decides.
mutations.find: argv = [str(AGY_GATE)]  # executed directly: the shebang decides

mutations.name: codex-launched-through-sys-executable
mutations._mechanism: The codex hook is driven by the suite's interpreter instead of PATH's python3.

mutations.name: shim-not-first-on-path
mutations._mechanism: The recording shim is not first on PATH, so the control reads no launch at all.

mutations.name: same-interpreter-run-not-skipped
mutations._mechanism: python3 == sys.executable no longer skips: a vacuous run reads as a pass.

mutations.name: absent-python3-not-skipped
mutations._mechanism: A missing python3 no longer skips with its reason.
